**Anastomoselækage** (anastomotic leakage) is a serious surgical complication that can occur following operations for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) [^src1]. Within the context of Danish healthcare quality monitoring, it has become a focal point for evaluating surgical outcomes and guiding clinical audits.

In the regional comments of the 2024 DANIBD annual report, [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]] explicitly advocated for the use of anastomoselækage as a primary quality metric [^src1]. The hospital argued that the re-operation rate is a poor indicator of surgical quality, noting that a patient may experience a poor postoperative condition due to the natural surgical stress response rather than an actual surgical failure [^src1]. Consequently, the hospital considers anastomotic leakage to be a much more relevant and accurate measure of quality, drawing parallels to cancer surgery where re-operation rates are similarly discounted [^src1]. This debate illustrates how the DANIBD registry functions not just as a national database, but as an active management tool for local quality improvements and process optimization in IBD treatment [^src1].
